description: CDEDI march turnout is described only as “dozens”; there is no reliable basis to decide whether at least 50 gathered.
required_followup: Seek an independent contemporaneous attendance estimate; do not convert “dozens” to a numeric threshold.

description: The Jan 26 transport protests are confirmed by three contemporary outlets, but none provides a people-count by site. Nyasa Times’ “over 100 police officers” is law-enforcement deployment, not protest attendance.
required_followup: Find event-specific crowd estimates for each site and resolve event scope before any city-level split.

description: The Guardian says “dozens” attended the Jan 28 FSWA march; numeric lower bound and >=50 threshold remain unresolved.
required_followup: Find independent turnout evidence; organization membership is not event attendance.

description: A Jan 21 Face of Malawi search-result article reports a Zomba street demonstration on Jan 20 and names demands/officials’ response, but web open failed with Cache miss and the body remains unreviewed. It provides no attendance figure.
required_followup: Retrieve the article body or find independent Zomba coverage; verify occurrence, attendance >=50 and precise state interaction.

description: The Jan 2 Malawi24 demonstration archive listing is search-only. Reader failure and ordinary HTTPS DNS failure prevented confirming whether AHL workers actually gathered on Jan 4. Jan 6 salary payment news does not confirm execution or cancellation.
required_followup: Locate contemporaneous follow-up proving occurrence or cancellation, then determine actual attendance, state target and whether earlier demonstrations continued into Jan.

description: AHL was reported as partly government-owned, but the Jan 4 plan concerned wages owed by the employer. No source establishes a demand addressed to the national government.
required_followup: Find original demands and identify the intended addressee; ownership alone does not establish domestic-state targeting.

description: Transport sources differ on an earlier agreement for three passengers per seat, the associations involved, and whether enforcement continued. The Nation says police tear gas dispersed some road-blocking groups and the action was called off, without one nationwide end time; Nyasa Times says MOAM southern leadership opposed limits, while Nation quotes MOAM’s national chair distancing the association.
required_followup: Trace the government/MDCA/MOAM statements and local reports. Preserve separate local end times if a single episode cannot be supported.

description: The Nation reports drivers/conductors throwing stones at motorists and cites a spokesperson’s claim that outsiders hijacked some actions. Nyasa Times separately reports attacks on kabaza operators at Bangwe. Target and attribution vary by report/site.
required_followup: Seek event-specific independent attribution and apply the codebook’s protester-violence definition without assuming all sites shared the conduct.

description: For the FSWA Lilongwe march, the District Commissioner declined to receive a petition and the group went to Lilongwe City Council. The later reception/outcome and event closure are not documented.
required_followup: Find whether City Council formally received/responded to the petition and whether the march ended there.

description: A Jan 26 Malawi24 item lists Mwanza and “other” sites; The Nation lists five districts/cities and says Mzuzu was unaffected. Evidence does not establish whether this was centrally coordinated as one national action or several local events.
required_followup: Compare local reports and union/association notices; do not split or merge solely from one broad national label.

description: The Jan 27 Nation report mentions a similar minibus protest in December 2020; it may be a prior distinct episode. The undated search result about Blantyre minibus owners may be another earlier action.
required_followup: Identify exact dates and physical continuity. Keep December outside Jan events unless a documented continuation fits the protocol.

description: AHL employees had reportedly demonstrated during arrears dating from Sep 2020, but Jan 11 reporting supplies no exact days; a November source also describes prior vigils. It is unresolved whether any campaign/action continued into January.
required_followup: Find dated event records and physical continuity; do not create a continuation without a known pre-January start.

description: Zomba has a reported Jan 20 local action and Lilongwe a Jan 28 FSWA march. A late-January Scrolla search result also says sex workers in different parts of the country took to streets on Jan 28 but identifies no other sites. Relationships/coordination remain unverified.
required_followup: Trace original local reporting and FSWA/local branch notices; identify any other Jan 28 sites and determine whether these were one national action or distinct local gatherings.

description: The Guardian and Nyasa Times provide distinct contemporary reports on Lilongwe. Southern African Herald explicitly republishes Nyasa Times; Dullah Omar cites Guardian; CIVICUS and VOA Afrique are later summaries. These are not four independent confirmations.
required_followup: Retain publisher/origin lineage and rely on the two distinct contemporary reports for cross-checking; trace any additional sources before counting independence.

description: Searches covered English national/local outlets and some Chichewa terms, but indexed results were dominated by English. Tumbuka and Chiyao were not systematically searched; rural and northern districts, local radio archives and regional-language sources may be underrepresented.
required_followup: Continue targeted local-language and regional media searches and record exact queries; do not treat sparse indexed results as absence.

description: Searches now include Jan 1–10, 11–20 and 21–31 date windows plus transport, traders, health/teachers, labor, Covid restrictions, sex workers and Chichewa terms; verified substantive reports cluster in Blantyre/Lilongwe, with Zomba and the Jan 26 transport action also represented. Other sectors and districts remain incompletely covered.
required_followup: Continue week-by-week local/regional searches for agriculture, markets, students, opposition, public-service labor and regional districts, then verify candidate bodies.

description: Reader Cache miss/internal errors on S003, S004, S011, S012, S023, S031, S033 and S034 were followed by ordinary HTTPS attempts for some URLs; DNS resolution failed for tested URLs. No site denial was observed. S033/S034 remain search-only.
required_followup: Retry only through ordinary authorized public retrieval when available; keep snippets as discovery evidence, not verified body text.

description: Official baseline/version, detailed original Coding Procedure and current comparison universe remain pending; no MM official IDs or integration decisions can be made in this unit.
required_followup: Coordinator to compare all unresolved candidates with authorized baseline and review policy before any official inclusion.

description: Some reported labor and transport tensions continued or were discussed after January, but the available Feb reporting concerns later teacher actions and does not establish January continuity for these candidates.
required_followup: Search dated February follow-up for physical continuation and preserve onset-based monthly ownership.

description: Two contemporary reports and a later VOA report place a quarantine riot at Mapanga on Jan 10. Face of Malawi quotes a prison spokesperson saying only “few individuals” perpetuated the riot but gives no number. The 518/approximately 600 arrivals are not event attendance.
required_followup: Find additional event-specific crowd estimates; do not substitute returnee cohort size. Coordinator should review fit for the original protest/riot scope.

description: Nyasa Times/Face and a later VOA account describe tear gas and damage; VOA reports about 20 escaped and 39 arrested/charged, while Face quotes a prison spokesperson saying no one had escaped at that point. The Nation later mentions arrests among returnees but does not link them to a particular date. Timing and event attribution remain unresolved.
required_followup: Review later corrections and independent accounts. Preserve timing/attribution; do not infer beatings or casualties from tear gas/property damage.

description: The Lilongwe District Commissioner refused to receive the FSWA petition and the group went to City Council; City Council receipt is unknown. The Guardian also quotes the Attorney General saying government would look at the issues and respond, after saying there was no immediate government comment. Event-level ignore/accommodation coding needs scoped review.
required_followup: Coordinator should distinguish the District Commissioner’s refusal from any later City Council/government response and apply the original accommodation/ignore definitions.
